documented_behavior:
Okta's March 2022 investigation post describes a January 2022 compromise of a third-party customer support engineer workstation with access to Okta support tooling, including the SuperUser application used to access customer tenants.
Okta's concluding investigation states the threat actor accessed active customer tenants within the SuperUser application during the controlled window.
mapping_assumptions:
AIT does not use Okta support logs. This reconstruction models SuperUser customer-tenant access as an undeclared /reconstruction/excess-scope/ path relative to a declared support-status allowlist endpoint.
Customer tenant identifiers observed via support tooling are represented with the synthetic sensitive marker customer_tenant_id.
Baseline covers an allowlisted support status check; mutated adds the reconstructed SuperUser tenant access path to induce behavioral divergence.

findings.evidence: Observed endpoint /reconstruction/excess-scope/superuser-tenant but it was not declared as expected.
findings.expected_behavior: Integration should stay within the declared endpoint allowlist.
findings.observed_behavior: Observed endpoint /reconstruction/excess-scope/superuser-tenant but it was not declared as expected.
findings.remediation_note: Reduce granted scopes and remove undeclared endpoint calls.
findings.title: Hidden endpoint access detected

findings.evidence: Additional endpoints were reached during the mutated run.
findings.expected_behavior: State changes should not unlock extra undeclared data access.
findings.remediation_note: Inspect state-dependent branches and scope checks in the integration.
findings.title: Mutated execution exposed additional behavior

findings.evidence: Response from /reconstruction/excess-scope/superuser-tenant contained a configured sensitive marker.
findings.expected_behavior: Sensitive marker fields should not be retrieved unless explicitly approved.
findings.remediation_note: Restrict the integration to minimum necessary fields and revalidate scopes.
findings.title: Sensitive marker accessed
